coverage.notes: This area is overwhelmingly high quality: almost every test exercises real espnet3/espnet2 code with mocking limited to legitimate external boundaries (torch.load/save I/O, torch.distributed, HfApi/urllib/tarfile network+archive calls, filesystem via tmp_path). Assertions consistently check real computed values (averaged tensors, decay math, rendered README text, aggregated stats counts, config-merge results) rather than mock call-was-made or tautological self-comparisons. The one substantive hollow-test issue found is the DummyDataset contract mismatch in test_collect_stats.py, which also exposes a real production bug (finding #1) -- confirmed by direct execution against the real CombinedDataset/collect_stats_batch, not just the dummy. Did not have budget to run further mutation spot-checks beyond the one that mattered (the collect_stats bug was proven by running the real SUT functions directly, which is stronger evidence than a source mutation). test_get_espnet_model in test_task_utils.py compares str(model) reprs of two independently constructed models -- weak in principle (repr ignores weight values) but still exercises the real construction path and would catch architecture-level regressions; not reported as a separate finding given time budget. Did not verify whether CollectStatsInferenceProvider.build_worker_setup_fn (the true Dask/remote worker init path) is exercised by the use_parallel=True parametrizations in test_collect_stats.py -- parallel.py/env_provider.py are outside this area's assigned files.

findings.summary: collect_stats_batch decides whether dataset[i] is a (uid, sample) tuple by checking dataset.use_espnet_preprocessor, but for the real CombinedDataset the tuple-vs-bare-value shape is controlled by a different, independent flag (use_espnet_collator), so a custom collate_fn silently corrupts or crashes stats collection.
findings.scenario: A recipe sets dataset use_espnet_preprocessor=True (any ESPnet AbsPreprocessor) and configures a custom, non-CommonCollateFn collate_fn in dataloader_config.collate_fn (a fully supported, Hydra-instantiable option per _build_collate_fn). CollectStatsInferenceProvider.build_env_local (L246-247) / build_worker_setup_fn (L271-272) then set dataset.use_espnet_collator = isinstance(collate_fn, CommonCollateFn) == False. Per CombinedDataset.__getitem__ (espnet3/components/data/dataset.py L205-212), dataset[i] then returns just the preprocessed sample dict, NOT a (uid, sample) tuple. But collect_stats_batch still takes the 'uid, sample = item' branch because it checks use_espnet_preprocessor (still True), not use_espnet_collator. Verified by direct execution: with a real CombinedDataset(use_espnet_preprocessor=True) and use_espnet_collator=False (the actual state in this scenario), dataset[0] returns {'speech': ..., 'text': ...}, and `uid, sample = item` silently unpacks the dict's own KEY NAMES as strings (uid='speech', sample='text') with no exception -- every uid and feature fed into feature-statistics aggregation for that stage is garbage. If the preprocessed sample dict does not have exactly 2 keys, a ValueError is raised instead (not a crash the caller would expect from a working collect_stats() call).
findings.suggested_fix: Branch on dataset.use_espnet_collator (the actual tuple-return gate), not dataset.use_espnet_preprocessor, in collect_stats_batch; or have _build_dataset force use_espnet_collator=True unconditionally for the stats-collection path regardless of the configured collate_fn's class (collect_stats_batch already builds its own structured_items list, so the outer collate_fn's expected input shape is irrelevant to how dataset[i] should be read).

findings.summary: DummyDataset.__getitem__ hardcodes the (uid,sample)-tuple decision on its own use_espnet_preprocessor constructor flag, mirroring collect_stats_batch's incorrect assumption instead of the real CombinedDataset contract (gated on the separate use_espnet_collator flag), so no parametrization of this test file can ever catch the mismatch in finding #1.
findings.scenario: test_collect_stats_local_basic and test_collect_stats_entrypoint_train/valid are parametrized over use_espnet_preprocessor and always use a custom DummyCollate (make_dataloader_cfg(use_custom_collate=True)) -- exactly the combination that triggers the real bug against CombinedDataset. But because DummyDataset's __getitem__ (not CombinedDataset) is the dataset under test, and it keys its tuple-return directly off use_espnet_preprocessor rather than modeling use_espnet_collator, the test suite exercises a self-consistent fake instead of the real contract, and passes regardless of whether collect_stats_batch's branch condition is correct.
findings.evidence: test_collect_stats.py:57-63 `if self.use_espnet_preprocessor: return uid, {...} else: return {...}` -- directly mirrors collect_stats.py's own (incorrect) branch condition instead of dataset.py's real use_espnet_collator gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace DummyOrganizer/DummyDataset with a real espnet3.components.data.dataset.CombinedDataset (as test_data_organizer.py and test_dataloader_builder.py already do) wired through _build_dataset/build_env_local, so the use_espnet_collator flag CollectStatsInferenceProvider actually sets is what governs dataset[i]'s shape; add a case with use_espnet_preprocessor=True + a custom (non-CommonCollateFn) collate_fn and assert on real, non-garbage uids and feature values.

findings.summary: collect_stats() rejects a dataloader config as soon as the mode's config merely HAS a multiple_iterator key (via hasattr), regardless of its value, so explicitly writing `multiple_iterator: false` (e.g. copied/adapted from an ESPnet2 config) raises the same 'ESPnet3 does not support multiple_iterator' RuntimeError as `multiple_iterator: true`.
findings.scenario: A user adapting an ESPnet2-style dataloader config to ESPnet3 keeps an explicit `train: {multiple_iterator: false, ...}` for clarity/documentation. collect_stats() then unconditionally raises RuntimeError even though the value clearly opts out of multiple-iterator mode, because `hasattr(mode_config, 'multiple_iterator')` is true for either boolean value. The identical hasattr-based pattern also exists in espnet3/components/data/dataloader.py:196 for the training dataloader path, so this is a systemic convention, not a one-off typo -- but the error message ('does not support multiple_iterator') reads as if it depends on the value being truthy, which will mislead users debugging the failure.
findings.evidence: collect_stats.py:549-551 `if mode_config is not None and hasattr(mode_config, 'multiple_iterator'): raise RuntimeError("ESPnet3 does not support multiple_iterator. ...")`. Confirmed by test/espnet3/utils/test_dataloader_builder.py::test_multiple_iterator_is_rejected and test/espnet3/components/data/test_collect_stats.py::test_collect_stats_rejects_multiple_iterator, both parametrized `[True, False]` and both expecting the RuntimeError in either case -- i.e. the tests correctly document this behavior as intentional, but neither the tests nor the error message make it clear to a config author that even an explicit `false` is rejected.
findings.suggested_fix: Either check the truthy value (`getattr(mode_config, 'multiple_iterator', False)`) so `multiple_iterator: false` is accepted, or -- if presence-of-key rejection really is intended -- reword the error to say 'the multiple_iterator key is not recognized by ESPnet3 in this location; remove it' rather than implying it depends on the boolean value.

findings.summary: test_ema_moves_ema_model_to_online_device sets up the move_ema_to_online_device branch (via a monkeypatched get_module_device simulating a device mismatch) but only asserts torch.isfinite(ema.ema_model.weight).all(), a property that would hold identically whether or not the move-to-device logic executes at all.
findings.scenario: If EMA.update()'s handling of move_ema_to_online_device were deleted entirely, or the branch that calls .to(device) on the EMA copy were silently skipped, the EMA weights computed on CPU would still be finite floats and the assertion would still pass -- the test does not check ema_model's device, nor compare against a value computed with the move disabled.
findings.evidence: test_ema.py:626-629 `with torch.no_grad(): net.weight.fill_(1.0)\n ema.update()\n assert torch.isfinite(ema.ema_model.weight).all()` -- no assertion on .device, and no differential comparison against the non-move code path.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert ema.ema_model's parameters/buffers end up on the device returned by the (mocked) online-model device sequence, or compare the updated weight against a hand-computed expected value that would only match if the move-then-update ordering is correct.
